description: The chart titled “QLoRA” presents a comparison of computational cost in terms of floating-point operations (FLOPs) across six fine-tuning approaches. The horizontal axis contains the method categories, shown as rotated labels in the order: Full FT, TAG, LoRA, MTL-FT, QLoRA, and Ours (there is no explicit x-axis label). The vertical axis is labeled “# FLOPs” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick marks at approximately \(10^{18}\), \(10^{19}\), and \(10^{20}\), spanning roughly from just under \(10^{18}\) up to slightly above \(10^{20}\). Each category is represented by a single vertical bar: Full FT is an orange bar reaching about \(6\times10^{19}\) FLOPs; TAG is orange at roughly \(4\times10^{19}\); LoRA is orange at around \(2.5\times10^{19}\); MTL-FT is orange near \(9\times10^{18}\) (just below \(10^{19}\)); QLoRA is orange around \(4\times10^{18}\); and Ours is a green bar at approximately \(4.5\times10^{18}\). The bars appear unstacked and ungrouped (one bar per method), with color used to visually distinguish “Ours” (green) from the other methods (orange), and there are no additional annotations or explicit sorting markers beyond the displayed left-to-right order.
